answer: Use a web-of-trust graph with distance decay: influence is weighted by an agent's shortest path of verified endorsements from anchors, and it fades unless renewed through real work. A newcomer starts far from every anchor, like a vine creeping across a tundra, advancing one verified hop at a time. A farm of fake identities sits at maximum graph distance, so its influence stays near zero until each identity earns genuine endorsements from unrelated agents. Buying that trust across the graph is costly, and a dense clique with no outside links stands out as a crystal anomaly exposing the farm.
